dossier.public_summary: The dip is deep, changes strongly from transit to transit and from sector to sector, and odd and even dips have very different depths. This matches two deep eclipses of a small star on the target (or a close binary) folded at half its period, not a 3-Earth-radius planet. The inconsistent depths and lack of repeating transits rule out a planet.

reasons.why: Strong odd/even depth difference indicates primary and secondary eclipses of an eclipsing binary folded at half the true period, not a planet at 12.3 d. Sector_oe_max_sigma=8.737 with 2 sectors over 3 sigma confirms it.

Depth changes dramatically between sectors and between individual transits (including negative depths), with signal dominated by 3 deep outliers out of 9 transits. Changes within a single source rule out calibration artefact.
reasons.value: p_constant=1.863e-19, depth_change_pct=237.5; transit_depths p_consistent=2.449627913942744e-48, share_of_top_3=0.984 with outliers at 12848, 11882, 13539 ppm

reasons.why: Very low planet rank as expected for binary/blend; centroid is inconclusive but no nearby star could plausibly reproduce the dip at this depth, pointing to on-target binary, while flat shape (v_sigma=-1.894) and duration ratio 1.068 do not favour planet - small-star eclipse on target is the best explanation.
